content: Low-grade fever refers to a mild elevation in body temperature that is either continuous or fluctuating, but it does not exceed 38.5 degrees Celsius (approximately 101 degrees Fahrenheit). This type of fever is considered a non-specific clinical finding, meaning it is not unique to a single condition but can be associated with a wide range of medical disorders. Low-grade fever may occur in the context of infectious diseases, such as viral infections or infective endocarditis. It can also be observed in autoimmune conditions, where the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues, or in malignant diseases, such as cancers. When a low-grade fever persists over time, it may serve as an indicator of an underlying illness that requires further investigation.
